title: Two Great Painters
author: James Baldwin
summary: 两位画家斗技：一个骗过鸟儿，另一个骗过了画家。
publicDomainBasis: Published 1912 by the American Book Company; author James Baldwin (1841–1925). Public domain in the United States and in China (author's life plus 70 years).

paragraphs.en: There was once a painter whose name was Zeuxis. He could paint pictures so lifelike that they were mistaken for the real things which they represented.
paragraphs.zh: 从前有一位画家，名叫宙克西斯。他画的画栩栩如生，常被人误以为是真的东西。

paragraphs.en: At one time he painted the picture of some fruit which was so real that the birds flew down and pecked at it. This made him very proud of his skill.
paragraphs.zh: 有一次，他画了一幅水果画，画得太逼真，鸟儿都飞下来啄食。这让他对自己的技艺非常自豪。

paragraphs.en: "I am the only man in the world who can paint a picture so true to life," he said.
paragraphs.zh: “我是世界上唯一能画得如此逼真的人。”他说。

paragraphs.en: There was another famous artist whose name was Parrhasius. When he heard of the boast which Zeuxis had made, he said to himself, "I will see what I can do."
paragraphs.zh: 还有一位著名画家，名叫帕拉修斯。他听说宙克西斯夸下海口，便对自己说：“我倒要看看我能做些什么。”

paragraphs.en: So he painted a beautiful picture which seemed to be covered with a curtain. Then he invited Zeuxis to come and see it.
paragraphs.zh: 于是他画了一幅美丽的画，画上似乎罩着一块帘子。然后他邀请宙克西斯来看。

paragraphs.en: Zeuxis looked at it closely. "Draw the curtain aside and show us the picture," he said.
paragraphs.zh: 宙克西斯仔细端详。“把帘子拉开，让我们看看画。”他说。

paragraphs.en: Parrhasius laughed and answered, "The curtain is the picture."
paragraphs.zh: 帕拉修斯笑着回答：“帘子就是画。”

paragraphs.en: "Well," said Zeuxis, "you have beaten me this time, and I shall boast no more. I deceived only the birds, but you have deceived me, a painter."
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”宙克西斯说，“这次你赢了我，我再也不夸口了。我只骗过了鸟儿，你却骗过了一位画家。”

paragraphs.en: Some time after this, Zeuxis painted another wonderful picture. It was that of a boy carrying a basket of ripe red cherries. When he hung this painting outside of his door, some birds flew down and tried to carry the cherries away.
paragraphs.zh: 过了一段时间，宙克西斯又画了一幅了不起的画：一个男孩提着一篮熟透的红樱桃。他把画挂在门外，一些鸟儿飞下来，想把樱桃叼走。

paragraphs.en: "Ah! this picture is a failure," he said. "For if the boy had been as well painted as the cherries, the birds would have been afraid to come near him."
paragraphs.zh: “唉！这幅画失败了，”他说，“因为要是那个男孩画得和樱桃一样好，鸟儿就不敢靠近他了。”
